clue.text: Lead poisoning primarily leads to backache

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the opening letter of the word before it is used

parts.note: the first letter of poisoning
lumbago is pain in the lower back

explanation.surface: A medical warning that lead poisoning first shows itself as back pain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lead poisoning' reads as one phrase, but Lead alone is the definition and 'leads to' only joins the wordplay to it.
explanation.definitionFit: Plumbago is an old name for graphite, the black lead of pencils, and also for the metal itself.

clue.text: Robert Lindsay?

definitions.note: a first name standing for the actor's surname
definitions.meaning: first meaning: the surname of the American actor Robert ...

definitions.note: a first name standing for the actress's surname
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the surname of the actress Lindsay ..., the Bionic Woman

explanation.walkthrough: Robert Lindsay is a British actor, so the clue looks like it wants him; split the name and each half is the first name of a different star sharing one surname.
explanation.definitionFit: Both the Hart to Hart actor Robert and the Bionic Woman actress Lindsay carry the surname Wagner.

clue.text: Woman's nether regions bitten by rodents

indicators.note: something bitten is held in the jaws of the biter, so one part sits inside the other

parts.note: mice are small rodents
the nether regions are the underworld, hell

explanation.surface: A slightly risqué image of a woman's lower body being nibbled by vermin.
explanation.walkthrough: Nether regions sounds anatomical, but here it means the underworld, the place below.
explanation.definitionFit: Michelle is a woman's first name, and the title of a Beatles song like several answers here.

clue.text: Function in which one's inducted into religious group

indicators.note: to be inducted into something is to be admitted inside it, so one part goes within another

parts.note: a sect is a religious group
an is the indefinite article, meaning one

explanation.surface: A ceremony in which a new member is admitted to a religious body.
explanation.walkthrough: Function sounds like an event or ceremony, matching the induction picture, but it is the mathematical sense; the 's after one is 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: The secant is a trigonometric function, the reciprocal of the cosine.

clue.text: Start of second half of year given a miss

definitions.text: Start of second half of year given a miss

parts.words: Start of second half of year given a miss
parts.note: surface reading: the month that opens the second half of the year is skipped; setter's reading: that month, named after Julius Caesar, is given a female form, made into a girl's name

explanation.surface: Someone decides to skip July altogether.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Given a miss' means skipped, but read it as 'made into a miss': the month named after Julius becomes the feminine name of the Julian family.
explanation.definitionFit: The feminine of Julius is a girl's name, as July is the masculine month named for Julius Caesar; it is also a Beatles song.

clue.text: Girl played a banjo topless? Not initially

indicators.note: a tune that is played can be improvised freely, suggesting letters rearranged
topless means with the top taken off, and in a down clue the top is the first letter

parts.note: the instrument, taken as written before its top letter is removed

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the opening letter of the word it follows is used

parts.note: the first letter of not
taken as written

explanation.surface: A girl strumming a banjo with no top on, apparently not at first.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the B from BANJO, add the N, and rearrange with A; amusingly, joanna is also rhyming slang for piano.
explanation.definitionFit: Joanna is a girl's first name; in Cockney rhyming slang it also means a piano.

clue.text: A killjoy like Harpagon getting left out

indicators.note: left out means omitted, and left also names the letter to drop

parts.note: Harpagon is the miser in Molière's comedy L'Avare
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A wet blanket compared to the stingy hero of a classic French comedy who gets excluded.
explanation.walkthrough: Harpagon, Molière's tight-fisted old man, is miserly; take out its L.
explanation.definitionFit: A misery is a gloomy person who spoils others' fun, a killjoy; it is also an early Beatles song.

clue.text: A new government installed in that old Asian city

indicators.note: something installed in a place is fitted inside it, so these letters go within another word

parts.note: yon is an archaic word for that
taken as written
N is the abbreviation for new
G is a standard abbreviation for government

explanation.surface: A fresh regime takes power in a historic city of Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old' looks like it describes the city, but 'that old' is the archaic word yon, which takes A, N and G inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Yangon, formerly Rangoon, is the largest city of Myanmar and was its capital until 2006.

clue.text: Source of 21 data in much of volume 1, curiously safe outside

indicators.note: the safe word sits outside the scrambled letters

parts.note: peter is old criminal slang for a safe

indicators.note: curiously signals letters arranged in an odd, unexpected order
most of the word, losing its last letter

parts.note: 1 is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Data source found in most of volume one, with a safe oddly placed outside.
explanation.walkthrough: The 21 in the definition is the puzzle's rain entry; peter is old safe-cracker slang for a safe.
explanation.definitionFit: A pluviometer is a rain gauge, the instrument that records rainfall figures.

clue.text: Government official put burden on staff

parts.note: to tax is to put a burden or strain on
to man is to staff, as in manning a desk

explanation.surface: A civil servant loads extra work on to employees.
explanation.walkthrough: Staff looks like a noun for employees, but it is the verb meaning to provide workers.
explanation.definitionFit: The taxman is the official who collects tax for the state; Taxman is also a Beatles song.

clue.text: The French king and queen once snubbed a singer of 2

parts.note: le is French for the
HM, His Majesty, is how a king is styled

indicators.note: snubbed suggests a nose cut short, so the word loses its end

parts.note: Queen Anne reigned 1702 to 1714

explanation.surface: French royals once cold-shouldered a performer of operatic music.
explanation.walkthrough: 2 is WAGNER, so the definition means a singer of Wagner's music; snubbed here means cut short, not ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: Lotte Lehmann was a celebrated German soprano, famous above all for Wagner roles such as Sieglinde.

clue.text: Indian national eating stale Indian bread

indicators.note: something eating another holds it inside, so the words before it contain the answer

parts.note: found across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A citizen of India munching on old naan.
explanation.walkthrough: Indian bread looks like naan, but bread is slang for money and stale means out of date: an obsolete coin.
explanation.definitionFit: The anna was a former Indian coin worth one sixteenth of a rupee, so it is money no longer current.

clue.text: Result of our violent rioting?

indicators.note: rioting suggests wild disorder, so the letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: What happens when we take to the streets in violent unrest.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does double duty: the wordplay rearranges two words, and the full sentence describes what such rioting brings about.
explanation.definitionFit: A revolution is the overthrow of a government, the outcome of a violent popular uprising; Revolution is also a Beatles song.

clue.text: Left with additional bit of silver in reserve capital

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship
more means additional

indicators.note: these words say which letters are picked from the word

parts.note: the first letter of silver
by means aside, in reserve, as in 'put by'

explanation.surface: Something left behind with an extra piece of silver kept back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reserve capital' sounds like money set aside; capital is the definition and 'in reserve' gives BY, as in putting money by.
explanation.definitionFit: Port Moresby is the capital city of Papua New Guinea.

clue.text: Harry quit pork? I must go out for a little bit

indicators.note: to harry is to harass, and the harassed letters are thrown into a new order
the letter I leaves and the letter a comes in to replace it

explanation.surface: Someone named Harry gives up pork, and I must leave for a while.
explanation.walkthrough: Change the I of QUIT PORK to A, giving QUAT PORK, then rearrange; 'Harry' looks like a name but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The top quark is an elementary particle, a tiny constituent of matter.

clue.text: By securing a third off, there's reason to celebrate

indicators.note: securing means holding fast, so this word grips the other letters within it

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: off means gone wrong or out of order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Getting a third knocked off a price gives cause for celebration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A third off' reads as a discount, but off is the signal to rearrange A THIRD inside BY.
explanation.definitionFit: A birthday is the yearly anniversary of one's birth, a standard occasion for celebration; Birthday is also a Beatles song.

clue.text: During audition, Mark traps instrument

indicators.note: an audition is a hearing, so the word is judged by how it is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a symbol is a mark or sign

explanation.surface: At a tryout, a musician called Mark catches out an instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: Traps looks like a verb, but it is jazz slang for a drum kit, so the definition is an instrument from the drum set.
explanation.definitionFit: A cymbal is the brass plate struck in a drum kit, which drummers call the traps.

clue.text: Bug used by US intelligence to catch blighter

indicators.note: to catch something is to hold it, so the other letters go within

parts.note: the CIA is the US Central Intelligence Agency
a cad, like a blighter, is a contemptible man

explanation.surface: The CIA plants a listening device to trap a scoundrel.
explanation.walkthrough: Bug sounds like a spy's listening device, which fits US intelligence, but here it is the insect.
explanation.definitionFit: The cicada is a loud chirping insect, and bug is a general word for an insect.

clue.text: Mike discovered the old writer residing in backward town producing made-up stories

parts.note: Mike is M in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: residing in a place means living inside it, so these letters go within the other word
backward means facing the other way, so the word is read from end to start

parts.note: a city is a large town

indicators.note: discovered means uncovered, with its covering taken off, so the outer letters are removed

parts.note: the word with its first and last letters removed
O is a standard abbreviation for old
Edgar Allan Poe, the American writer

explanation.surface: A cryptic tale of a man called Mike tracking down an elderly author living in a sleepy town.
explanation.walkthrough: Discovered seems to mean found, but it means stripped of its cover, so only the middle letter of 'the' survives.
explanation.definitionFit: Mythopoeic means myth-making, giving rise to myths and invented stories.

clue.text: Queen of the witches can't stand going round the City

indicators.note: going round something means encircling it, so this word wraps the other letters

parts.note: to hate is to be unable to stand something
EC is the postcode area of the City of London

explanation.surface: A witch queen who detests London's financial district.
explanation.walkthrough: The City is London's financial district, whose postal district is EC (East Central).
explanation.definitionFit: Hecate is the Greek goddess of magic and witchcraft, appearing as queen of the witches in Macbeth.

clue.text: Charles invests in bonds

indicators.note: to invest literally means to clothe or wrap, so this word surrounds the other

parts.note: Chas is the short form of Charles
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man named Charles puts his money into bonds.
explanation.walkthrough: Invests and bonds suggest finance, but invests means wraps round, and bonds are physical restraints.
explanation.definitionFit: Chains are fetters or restraints, things that bind, so they are bonds; Chains is also an early Beatles cover.

clue.text: Now and then Croatians spit, possibly …

indicators.note: now and then means at intervals, so only every other letter of the next word is kept

parts.note: the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters of this word

explanation.surface: Croatians occasionally spitting, which the ellipsis carries on into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: Spit here is a light shower, not spittle; 'possibly' marks it as one example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A spit is a few scattered drops of precipitation, a light form of the weather the answer names; Rain is also a Beatles song.

clue.text: … on account of us backing cases in competition

indicators.note: in means placed within, so these letters sit inside the word for competition

parts.note: a bee is a contest, as in a spelling bee

indicators.note: backing means supporting from behind, so the word before it goes after the other piece

parts.note: CA is read here as a short form of cases
taken as written

explanation.surface: Continuing the last clue: something happens because we are funding lawsuits in a contest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cases in competition' sounds like competition law, but competition is a spelling bee; the ellipsis ties the surface to the previous clue without sharing any wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Because is the conjunction meaning for the reason that, which the phrase on account of also expresses; it is a Beatles song too.

clue.text: A quiet crowd meditate here?

parts.note: taken as written
sh is the call for quiet
to ram is to cram or crowd in

explanation.surface: A hushed throng gathers, perhaps to meditate.
explanation.walkthrough: Crowd reads as a noun for a gathering, but it is the verb meaning to pack in.
explanation.definitionFit: An ashram is a Hindu religious retreat where people go to meditate; the Beatles famously stayed at one in Rishikesh.

clue.text: American volumes in Irish mostly

parts.note: a fire that is in is lit, still burning

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: Erse is the Irish Gaelic language

explanation.surface: Measures of liquid in an Irish setting, according to Americans.
explanation.walkthrough: In looks like a link word, but it means alight, as a fire is 'still in'; American signals the US spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Liters, the US spelling of litres, are metric units of volume.

clue.text: Horny type from New York state getting half-cut

parts.note: NY is the abbreviation for New York

indicators.note: half-cut means with half cut away, so only the first half of the word remains

parts.note: Alaska is a US state

explanation.surface: A randy New Yorker getting drunk, half-cut being British slang for tipsy.
explanation.walkthrough: Horny suggests lust and half-cut drunkenness, but the horns are literal and half-cut chops a word in two.
explanation.definitionFit: The nyala is a southern African antelope whose males have long spiralled horns.
